topic: The Bridge Between Slopes and Areas: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus

outline.topic: The Bridge Between Slopes and Areas: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Geometric Intuition
sections.content: Briefly recall that a derivative represents the instantaneous slope of a curve, while an integral represents the accumulated area under the curve. Visualize a line graph transitioning from a single point to a shaded region.
sections.example: Visual: A squirrel climbing a hill. The derivative is the steepness of the climb; the integral is the total elevation gained.

sections.title: The Inverse Relationship: Integration vs. Differentiation
sections.content: Introduce the core concept: Integration and differentiation are inverse operations, much like addition and subtraction. Define the accumulation function F(x) = ∫[a to x] f(t) dt.
sections.example: Visual: An animation of a 'factory machine' where a function goes in, gets differentiated, and the 'inverse machine' integrates it to return to the original function.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1)
sections.content: Explain that the derivative of an accumulation function is the original function itself (d/dx ∫[a to x] f(t) dt = f(x)). This links the 'rate of change' to the 'accumulated area'.
sections.example: Visual: A filling water tank. The rate at which the water level rises (derivative) corresponds exactly to the current flow rate (the original function).

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 2)
sections.content: Show the practical computation method: ∫[a to b] f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a), where F is the antiderivative. This simplifies complex area calculations into simple subtraction.
sections.example: Visual: Calculating the total distance a robotic turtle travels by subtracting its position at time 'a' from its position at time 'b'.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
sections.content: Summarize the 'Bridge': We no longer need to manually sum infinite rectangles to find area; we simply find the antiderivative and evaluate at boundaries.
sections.example: Visual: A 'bridge' graphic connecting the 'Derivative Island' and the 'Integral Island', emphasizing that the Fundamental Theorem is the link between them.

lecture_lines: Integral is the total accumulated area.

Highlight the area under the curve in blue (#0000FF).

Show the rectangle scaling to emphasize the sum of areas.
Change rectangle color to gold (#FFD700) to show accumulation.

storyboard.title: The Inverse Relationship: Integration vs. Differentiation
animations: Show f(x) and its derivative f'(x) side-by-side.
Animate f(x) slope tangent line tracking the curve.
Fade out tangent line and fade in integral area.

storyboard.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1)
lecture_lines: This is fundamental theorem part one.
animations: Show an area growing as x increases to the right.
Label the start point a and endpoint x.
Transition F(x) to show it is a function.
Highlight the relationship between F'(x) and f(x).

storyboard.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 2)
animations: Show two distinct points a and b on x-axis.
Animate the area filling between a and b.

storyboard.title: Synthesis and Summary
animations: Synthesize integral and derivative symbols in one frame.
Flash symbols to show their inverse operations nature.
Final screen showing the full elegant relationship formula.
